function.name: ALLOC
function.param: Size in bytes of the memory zone to reserve

description.p: It reserves a memory zone and returns a pointer to the same one. This is a advanced function, so that it is good to know the concept of POINTER before using it. That memory zone can have random data or rest of a previous use and it is responsability of the programmer to initialize it.

The pointer returned by ALLOC can be assigned to any variable of type POINTER, e.g. byte pointer or int pointer. It is recommended to save the pointer in a global variable and to access to the memory using the operator [] in the program.

If you can not reserve the given memory, alloc generates an error in runtime, however it is not often to happen, because the operating system can use the free space of hard disk to create swap memory to solve it.

The number of elements that will have in the new reserved memory zone will be equivalent to the total size divided by the size of each element for the type of pointer used. To reserve space for 1000 bytes we need 1000 bytes, but to reserve space for 1000 ints we need to reserve 4000 bytes, 1000 * 4 bytes, that is the value returned by sizeof(int).
The pointer returned by alloc must be saved it so it is necessary use it with the function , to can use again the used memory.
